url_length.description: Total character length of the normalized URL.
url_length.rationale: Phishing URLs frequently use unusually long paths and query strings to camouflage lures or embed redirect links.

hostname_length.rationale: Long hostnames often conceal spoofed brand names within deep subdomains.

path_length.description: Character length of the URL path component.
path_length.rationale: Deep directory paths or embedded filenames often simulate authentic corporate portals.

query_length.description: Character length of the URL query string.
query_length.rationale: Complex query strings may carry base64-encoded parameters or victim identifiers.

dot_count.description: Total number of dot (.) characters in the URL.
dot_count.rationale: Excessive dots typically indicate multiple subdomain layers or deceptive domain names.

hyphen_count.description: Total number of hyphen (-) characters in the URL.
hyphen_count.rationale: Hyphens are widely used in spoofed domain names (e.g., 'paypal-security-update').

underscore_count.description: Total number of underscore (_) characters in the URL.
underscore_count.rationale: Underscores are uncommon in legitimate domains but appear in script parameters and phishing paths.

slash_count.description: Total number of forward slash (/) characters in the URL.
slash_count.rationale: High slash counts indicate nested paths or path-traversal redirect constructs.

question_mark_count.description: Number of question marks (?) in the URL.
question_mark_count.rationale: Legitimate URLs contain at most one delimiter for query parameters; multiple question marks indicate anomalies.

equal_count.description: Number of equal sign (=) characters in the URL.
equal_count.rationale: Multiple key-value parameters are common in session tracking and tracking redirects.

at_count.description: Number of @ characters in the URL.
at_count.rationale: The @ symbol treats preceding characters as user authentication credentials, masking the true host.

ampersand_count.description: Number of ampersand (&) characters in the URL.
ampersand_count.rationale: Represents the density of parameters passed in the query string.

percent_count.description: Number of percent (%) characters in the URL.
percent_count.rationale: Percent encoding is used to obfuscate characters and bypass naive pattern matchers.

digit_count.description: Total number of numeric digits in the URL.
digit_count.rationale: Phishing URLs often incorporate generated numeric IDs, IP addresses, or hash digests.

digit_ratio.description: Proportion of numeric digits relative to total URL length.
digit_ratio.rationale: Elevated digit proportions suggest automated domain generation or algorithmic parameters.

special_char_count.description: Count of non-alphanumeric characters excluding standard URL delimiters.
special_char_count.rationale: Unusual punctuation marks, symbols, and operators correlate with malicious payload strings.

has_ip_host.description: Binary flag indicating whether the host is an IPv4 or IPv6 address.
has_ip_host.rationale: Direct IP hosting is a strong red flag; legitimate services rarely ask users to browse directly to raw IPs.

has_https.description: Binary flag indicating whether the URL protocol is HTTPS.
has_https.rationale: Lack of HTTPS indicates unencrypted transport, though modern phishing also adopts free TLS certificates.

has_at_symbol.description: Binary indicator for the presence of the '@' userinfo separator.
has_at_symbol.rationale: Direct indicator of browser userinfo spoofing attempts.

subdomain_count.description: Number of subdomain labels separated by dots.
subdomain_count.rationale: Deep subdomain chains allow attackers to create spoof domains like 'paypal.com.attacker.com'.

is_shortened.description: Binary flag indicating whether the domain belongs to a known URL shortener.
is_shortened.rationale: Shorteners mask destination domains and circumvent reputation filters.

char_entropy.description: Shannon character entropy of the URL string.
char_entropy.rationale: High entropy signifies randomness, DGA (Domain Generation Algorithms), or encoded payloads.

suspicious_keyword_count.description: Count of keywords associated with credential harvesting and banking lures.
suspicious_keyword_count.rationale: Attackers frequently rely on urgency words ('login', 'verify', 'account', 'update') in paths.

has_abused_tld.description: Binary flag indicating whether the TLD is on the high-abuse registration list.
has_abused_tld.rationale: Free and low-cost TLDs (e.g., .tk, .xyz, .buzz) have high historical abuse concentrations.

has_double_slash_path.description: Binary flag indicating '//' in the URL path component.
has_double_slash_path.rationale: Double slashes in paths can induce client-side redirection vulnerabilities.

has_punycode.description: Binary flag indicating punycode ('xn--') in hostname.
has_punycode.rationale: Punycode enables internationalized domain name (IDN) homograph attacks spoofing similar characters.

param_count.rationale: High parameter counts are typical in tracking, redirection, and token-passing scripts.

fragment_length.description: Character length of the URL fragment (#).
fragment_length.rationale: Client-side fragments are rarely sent to servers but can execute client script payloads.

longest_token_length.description: Length of the longest contiguous alphanumeric segment in the URL.
longest_token_length.rationale: Excessively long alphanumeric tokens reflect hashes, session IDs, or encoded payloads.
